tasks.short: Review design documents for code compliance.

steps.what: List applicable government or industrial codes and standards cited.

loop.purpose: Attach each stated requirement to the standard clause identifier it names.
loop.input: A requirement sentence and the identifiers in the document.
loop.output: A row with a clause id, or a gap.
loop.check: The clause id appears in the document.
loop.stop: Stop when a requirement row has no clause id.
loop.why_not_simpler: A present-or-absent checklist cannot attach a free-text requirement to the standard clause identifier it names.

steps.what: Review civil design, engineering, and construction technical documentation for compliance.
Record which requirements and regulations the review must still ensure.

tasks.design: Applicable government or industrial codes and standards cited in the file are listed from {DOCS}. The manager reviews the civil design, engineering, and construction technical documentation and judges compliance. A requirement with no clause id is not treated as met. The list does not find the design compliant. The manager records what the review must still ensure.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cited standards were buried in long documents, so a review could miss the clause.
tasks.enabler_now: A cited identifier can be listed. The manager still reads the design against it.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the design meets the code is a technical judgement. A listed identifier is not that judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides compliance. The clause list only shows what the document cites.
tasks.altitude: Compliance stays with the manager. A listed code is a citation, not a finding.

reach.task: Check a document against a cited obligation.
reach.learn: A listed identifier is not a pass.

evidence.claim: Cited code identifiers can be listed from a document the company holds. The list does not decide compliance.
A requirement with no clause identifier is a gap in the citation, not a statement that the design fails or passes.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A wind development manager in a mid-size European company. A project list does not direct work, award a contract, or decide a permit.
Fields: A document id is required. A requirement row needs a clause id or it stays a gap. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the development manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: The manager writes the compliance note. The list does not say the design passes.
unknowns: Whether the company holds the text of the cited standard or only the identifier.
research_questions: Which reviews still rely on a printed code book that is not in the document store?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the documents and recording the gaps stay with the manager.

incremental.description: Check the clause list is for the document version under review.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes cited standards have no identifier, so the manager searches the document by hand. High assumes each requirement names a clause id and the manager spends the time on the compliance judgement. The judgement is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assemble scope, quantities, and dates from the approved plan.
Draft request sentences that each cite a plan quantity or date.

loop.purpose: Bind each request sentence to a scope, quantity, or date id.
loop.input: A sentence and the approved plan.
loop.output: The sentence with an id, or a gap.
loop.check: The id is on the approved plan, and the quantity matches.
loop.stop: Stop when a sentence states a quantity the plan does not hold.
loop.why_not_simpler: A boilerplate request cannot tell which sentence states a quantity the approved plan does not hold.

steps.what: Prepare the project commercial terms and accept the text.
Issue requests for proposals for construction or equipment acquisition.

tasks.design: Scope, quantities, and dates are assembled from the approved plan in {PROJECT}. Request sentences are drafted only where each one cites a plan id. The manager prepares the commercial terms and accepts the text. {EMAIL} issues the request for construction or equipment acquisition only for that accepted version. A quantity the plan does not hold is not drafted.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were copied from the last project, and quantities drifted from the current plan.
tasks.enabler_now: The approved plan can supply quantities and dates, and a sentence that invents a quantity can be stopped.
tasks.still_hard: Commercial terms, risk, and whether the text is fair to issue are the manager's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager writes the commercial terms and accepts the request before it is issued.
tasks.altitude: The issued request is the version the manager accepted. The draft only repeats the plan.

reach.task: Issue a request for construction proposals.
reach.learn: Suppliers see the accepted text, not the first draft.

evidence.claim: A request can reuse scope, quantities, and dates from a plan the manager has already accepted. It cannot set the commercial terms.
Generated text issued to suppliers is reviewed by the manager before issue. EU AI Act article 50 expects disclosure or a person's review when generated content informs others.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A wind development manager in a mid-size European company. A project list does not direct work, award a contract, or decide a permit.
Fields: A plan id and a quantity id are required on every drafted sentence. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the development manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: Commercial terms are written by the manager. The draft does not add them.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the development manager.
unknowns: Whether suppliers receive the request through a portal or by mail.
research_questions: Which quantities in past requests were typed rather than taken from the plan?

already_counted.description: Writing the commercial terms and accepting the request stay with the manager.

incremental.description: Read the draft against the plan before accepting the commercial terms.

approvals.approved_version: request version and the plan ids it cites

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes the plan has no quantity ids, so the manager writes the request by hand. High assumes boilerplate sentences cite the plan and the manager writes the commercial terms. Issue waits for acceptance.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Pull the named question on the wind farm projects.
Provide technical support for design, construction, or commissioning.
Write the answer given and the record it used.

tasks.design: The design, construction, or commissioning question is pulled from {PROJECT} with the record it names in {DOCS}. The manager provides the technical support. A question with no record id is not given a pack. The pack does not answer the question. The manager writes the answer that was given.
tasks.previous_blocker: The drawing or commissioning record was hard to find while the question was being asked.
tasks.enabler_now: The named record can be pulled before the manager answers.
tasks.still_hard: The technical answer depends on the design and on what is happening on site.
tasks.human_edge: The manager gives the support. A retrieved record is not an answer.
tasks.altitude: Technical support stays with the manager. The pack only shows the record the question named.

reach.task: Support commissioning on an operating farm.
reach.learn: The record is the evidence. The answer is the manager's.

evidence.claim: The drawing or commissioning record named in a question can be pulled from the store. It does not answer the question.
Technical support during construction or commissioning is the manager's judgement. A retrieved page is not that support.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A wind development manager in a mid-size European company. A project list does not direct work, award a contract, or decide a permit.

Fields: A question id and a record id are required. A question with no record is answered without a pack. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the development manager finishes it by hand.
Native check: The answer is written by the manager. The pack is not rewritten into an answer.
unknowns: Whether commissioning questions arrive from the contractor or from the owner's engineer.
research_questions: Which answers are still given on site and never tied back to a record id?

already_counted.description: Giving the technical answer and writing it down stay with the manager.

incremental.description: Check the pulled record is the drawing the question named.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes the question names no record, so the manager searches while answering. High assumes the named record is pulled first. The technical answer is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The development manager still judges whether a design meets the code, still writes the commercial terms of a request for proposals, and still answers the technical question. A cited clause can be listed. A quantity can be copied from the plan.
reach: Compliance managers match a document to a cited obligation, and this job learns a listed code is not a finding of compliance.
Construction managers issue a request for proposals from an agreed scope, and this job learns the request goes out only after the manager accepts the text.
skills_to_grow: Read a cited code identifier and still decide whether the design meets it.
Accept request text only where each quantity cites the plan.
Answer a commissioning question from the record, in the manager's own words.
role.ambitious_version: A request for proposals leaves the company only as the version the manager accepted, and a code review ends with the manager's own note of what still fails.
